::: {.why}
Whether a stylized fact survives aggregation decides at what horizon you are allowed to use Gaussian machinery, and the answer is further out than most people assume.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report how kurtosis falls with horizon in your data and compare it against what the central limit theorem would give for independent draws.
- Say at what horizon a normal approximation becomes defensible for your series, and what still breaks at that horizon.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>50 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Extend last night's four numbers: compute kurtosis, the 1st and 99th percentile in standard deviations, and the largest standardised move at each of the four horizons. Then simulate iid draws from the daily empirical distribution and aggregate them the same way. The gap between your real series and the shuffled one is the contribution of dependence rather than of the marginal distribution.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} State the conclusion in the notebook as a rule you will follow: at what horizon you will use normal approximations, at what horizon you will not, and which quantity remains non-normal at every horizon you looked at.
:::
:::
